root_cause.text: The loop condition in `nvme_dbbuf_set` uses `<=` instead of `<` when iterating through queue indices, causing an out-of-bounds array access when `i` equals `dev->online_queues`, which is a count rather than a valid index.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 547 from `for (i = 1; i <= dev->online_queues; i++)` to `for (i = 1; i < dev->online_queues; i++)`. The CVE description explicitly states that "dev->online_queues is a count incremented in nvme_init_queue. Thus, valid indices are 0 through dev->online_queues − 1." The KASAN splat confirms a read beyond the allocated 1152-byte region, occurring when the loop accesses `dev->queues[dev->online_queues]`, which is one element past the valid range.

candidates.rationale: The loop condition uses `<=` instead of `<`, causing the loop to iterate one extra time when i equals dev->online_queues. Since dev->online_queues is a count (not a valid index), accessing dev->queues[dev->online_queues] results in an out-of-bounds array access. vuln_statements.explanation: The loop condition uses `<=` instead of `<` when iterating through queue indices. Since `dev->online_queues` is a count (representing the number of queues) rather than a valid array index, the condition `i <= dev->online_queues` causes the loop to execute one extra iteration when `i` equals `dev->online_queues`. This results in an out-of-bounds array access when attempting to dereference `dev->queues[dev->online_queues]`. The correct condition should be `i < dev->online_queues` to ensure `i` never exceeds the maximum valid index.
